title: Majestic: Win the Race with a Pawn Mate
summary: Let Black promote first: the trapped rook and king leave a mating square for White’s c-pawn.

nodes.question: Does Black’s faster promotion decide the race?
nodes.explanation: Black’s king on b8 and rook on a8 are boxed in by a7 and White’s a6 pawn. Kd7 protects c7 and controls c8. This seven-piece position is reconstructed after the forced ...b3 between the saved 132- and 133-second diagrams.

branches.title: Source idea: ignore the promotion race and deliver pawn mate
commentary: Begin after the forced ...b3 in the later seven-piece phase. The preceding rook offer, king walk and capture sequence remain source context outside this verification.
c5 advances toward the mating square c7. It is the only winning move in this exact position. White must spend this tempo advancing the pawn while keeping Kd7 in place.
b2 is Black’s only legal move. Ra8 is blocked by its own king and a7 pawn; Ka8, Ka7, Kb7, Kc7 and Kc8 are occupied or controlled, and a7 is blocked by a6.
c6 keeps the mating plan. White does not need to promote first because c7 itself will check the black king.
b1=Q promotes before White, as shown in the clip. The new queen on b1 does not control c7 and cannot answer the coming adjacent pawn check.
c7# is actual checkmate. Kd7 protects c7 and controls c8, a6 controls b7, and Black’s own rook and pawn occupy a8 and a7. No queen interposition can block a pawn’s adjacent attack on b8.
branches.explanation: c7# is actual checkmate. Kd7 protects c7 and controls c8, a6 controls b7, and Black’s own rook and pawn occupy a8 and a7. No queen interposition can block a pawn’s adjacent attack on b8.

branches.title: Independent defense: underpromote instead
commentary: Independently replace the source’s queen promotion with a knight promotion. The earlier moves follow the same selected race.
c5 keeps the king and rook sealed in their cage.
b2 remains the only legal Black move in this exact diagram.
c6 threatens c7 mate, regardless of the promotion-piece choice.
b1=N tries a different new piece. The knight on b1 cannot capture c7, shield b8 from a pawn attack, or give check to Kd7.
c7# is still actual mate. Underpromotion does not change the cage or remove the mating pawn.

branches.title: Independent error: move the king instead of the pawn
commentary: Independently compare a king move that looks active but abandons the essential mating geometry.
Kd6 changes a forced win into a forced loss. The king no longer controls c8 or protects the eventual c7 pawn, releasing the black king.

b2 is a representative winning reply. Black can promote without facing the original c7 mate, while Kb8 also gains legal escapes. This stops at a checked losing position for White rather than claiming that promotion itself is immediate mate.

exercises.prompt: Why is it safe to let Black get a queen first?
exercises.answer: The winning threat is c7 mate, not promotion. A new queen on b1 cannot capture the adjacent checking pawn or create an escape square for its king.

exercises.prompt: What is White’s king contributing from d7?
exercises.answer: It protects c7 and controls c8. The illustrated Kd6 error releases c8; other king moves can also waste the tempo needed for the pawn race. Every king move from this root gives up the forced win.

The bridge is explicitly reconstructed rather than claimed as a separately captured frame. The earlier eleven-piece rook/knight sacrifices and king walk remain unverified source context.
